result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_forest()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is a forest. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4140-L4220){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_forest() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A forest is an acyclic, undirected graph (disjoint union of trees). For a graph with *n* nodes and *k* connected components to be a forest it: - must be undirected - must have exactly *n - k* edges - must be acyclic ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if graph is a forest, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A tree is a special case of a forest with k=1 (single component). ## Examples {.doc-examples} A single tree already satisfies the forest definition, since a tree is just a forest with one component: ::: {#f41974ef .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec tree = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) tree.is_forest() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Unlike `is_tree()`, this doesn't require a single connected component -- several disjoint trees together still form a forest: ::: {#0a1b0140 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} forest = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") # first tree .add_edge("C", "D") # second, disjoint tree ) forest.is_forest(), forest.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: A cycle breaks the "acyclic" requirement, so it's neither a forest nor a tree: ::: {#0865ad9b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} cycle = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) cycle.is_forest() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: An empty graph vacuously satisfies the definition too: ::: {#30c7cabc .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph(directed=False).is_forest() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: :::
